# Errors and validation

<!-- Generated by `npm run train` from the sources each rule cites. To change a rule for good, change its source or say so in training/feedback.md; the next training run regenerates this file. -->

- **Fail closed on a value that is present but invalid. Never treat a malformed field, header, directive line or forwarded certificate as absent. Reject a parameter, option or request field the code doesn't honor (with 400 at an API) instead of accepting it and dropping it.** Ignoring malformed or unhonored input hides errors, weakens security controls, and reports success for intent that was thrown away. *Check:* Look for parse failures that fall back to the 'not provided' path, optional-directive matches where a malformed line falls through to default behavior, decoders that partly accept input, and handler branches that validate a field and then build the downstream request without it. <sub>Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity ADR-1172; Identity ADR-1403; Identity outcomes of #551; Identity ADR-1068; project-template outcomes of #149</sub>
- **Reject input or configuration that names an unregistered member of a vocabulary (strategy, profile, method, provider, format), or that sits at a scope that never reads it, and throw or answer 400 with an error that names it. Never skip it, return a default or apply a no-op.** A name nobody registered, or a setting stored where nothing reads it, otherwise fails silently, and a security requirement the operator configured is never enforced. *Check:* Look for lookups by name that return null, an empty result or a no-op when nothing matches, and for settings parsing that ignores unknown keys or filters out entries that don't apply to the current scope. <sub>Identity ADR-1150; Identity ADR-1140; Identity ADR-1149; Identity ADR-1190; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Reject a settings or configuration document that cannot be honored wherever it enters (configuration, management API, registration, stored read): an unconvertible value, a list written as a scalar or the reverse, a non-object document, or null for a setting with no default. Never load it partially or store it.** Configuration accepted without being honored is invisible failure. *Check:* Look for settings parsing that catches conversion failures and continues, treats a non-object document as `{}`, or accepts scalar/list mismatches. An empty array must configure an empty list, not be rejected. <sub>Identity ADR-1139</sub>
- **When code reads remote or external state (an API, a CLI, a file, a git command), treat only a definite answer as negative. Treat only an explicit not-found (for example HTTP 404, or `git ls-remote --exit-code` returning 2) as absent, and report and stop on any other failure (auth error, 5xx, network, unreadable body, other exit code). For `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, only exit 1 means 'not an ancestor'.** A transient failure read as 'no' or 'missing' leads to destructive or wrong actions, such as deleting a branch or reporting a branch as unprotected, based on an answer nobody gave. *Check:* Look for existence probes and API/CLI calls whose failure branch (non-zero exit, catch, parse failure) leaves a flag at its false default and then acts on it, especially when stderr is sent to null and only zero vs non-zero is tested. <sub>project-template outcomes of #129; project-template outcomes of #146; Identity review of #420; project-template outcomes of #291; project-template outcomes of #310; project-template outcomes of #326</sub>
- **Don't turn a failure to read, parse or decode input into a value that looks like valid empty content or zero. Return a distinct failure or an explicit 'unknown', warn with the source's path, and treat a success status whose body is empty, null, not JSON or the wrong shape as a read failure.** Callers can't tell unreadable input from empty input, so results built from missing data, such as a cost of 0 or a user who seems signed out, are reported as successful. *Check:* Look for catch blocks or fallbacks that return '', an empty collection, 0 or a signed-out result on parse failure, and for parsed responses (`ConvertFrom-Json`, `JsonSerializer.Deserialize`) used without checking for null or the wrong shape after a success status. <sub>project-template outcomes of #331; project-template outcomes of #272; project-template outcomes of #147; project-template outcomes of #225; Identity outcomes of #600</sub>
- **Make a security control that depends on a shared store (brute-force or failed-attempt limiter, replay cache, session lookup) fail closed: an unreachable store throws, and an add with an expiry that isn't in the future fails. Make only a capacity guard such as a request-rate or quota limiter fail open, with a short per-call timeout and a circuit breaker, logging a warning and not billing usage it didn't count.** A store outage must not lift a security control, but it also must not turn into a service outage through a capacity guard. *Check:* In limiters and replay or session checks, look for catches around store calls that return 'not limited', success or absent for a security guard, and for capacity guards that refuse on store errors or have no short timeout or breaker. *Note:* Don't report a correctness limiter (brute force, replay, password attempts) for failing closed without a breaker. Don't ask a distributed rate limiter to fail open when its design records say failures throw on purpose; the host can catch and admit. <sub>Identity ADR-1164; Identity ADR-1237; Identity ADR-1246; Identity ADR-1198; Identity outcomes of #547; coordination outcomes of #22</sub>
- **When a session or shared-state store is unavailable, answer 503 through a dedicated store-unavailable exception. Never answer 401, return an anonymous principal or treat the session as missing.** A 401 for an outage logs users out or sends frontends into a login loop, and it hides the outage. *Check:* Look at catch blocks around session-store reads and lease operations that return 401, sign out, fall through to a challenge or treat the request as anonymous. <sub>Identity ADR-1290; Identity ADR-1292; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md</sub>
- **A loop that periodically revalidates a signed-in session or long-lived connection fails closed. It logs and retries while the store is only unavailable, signs the user out on any other unexpected failure, and exits only on its own cancellation.** If one unexpected error stops revalidation, a session that has ended or been revoked stays signed in for the life of the connection. *Check:* In revalidation loops, look for catches that keep the user signed in or end the loop on general exceptions, that treat a store outage as the session ending, or that treat any OperationCanceledException as shutdown. <sub>Identity ADR-1435; Identity ADR-1441; Identity outcomes of #600</sub>
- **When several candidates (selection rules, tenants matching a host) match where one is expected, fail closed: throw, or resolve to 'no match'. Never silently pick the first one.** Picking one arbitrarily can bind the request to the wrong client, tenant or session namespace. *Check:* Look for FirstOrDefault or First over multiple possible matches without an ambiguity check, and for Single that would turn one bad row into a server error on every request. <sub>Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md; Identity ADR-1165</sub>
- **When a required configured value such as an issuer is missing, fail with an error that names the setting to configure. Don't fall back to a value taken from the request (scheme and host) or another guess.** A request-derived fallback is an unvalidated second source of a security-relevant value. *Check:* Look for null-coalescing or fallback branches that use the request origin or a hard-coded value when configuration or stored data is missing. <sub>Identity ADR-1165; Identity ADR-1182</sub>
- **Never silently destroy or regenerate data on failure. Run a destructive self-heal or reset only on the specific exception that proves the data is unreadable (such as a `CryptographicException` from unwrapping), and make a recoverable-unavailability exception not derive from a type that cleanup code handles by deleting data. When a stored protected payload can't be unprotected, fail or treat it as absent with a warning, and never fall back to reading it as plaintext.** An outage or a revoked key must not trigger deletion, and a plaintext fallback would accept a forged record. *Check:* Look for heal, prune or reset code that catches `Exception` broadly, new unavailability exceptions derived from `CryptographicException`, catch blocks that regenerate or delete keys that can't be read outside an explicit development opt-in, and unprotect failures that fall through to plaintext deserialization. <sub>Identity ADR-1247; Identity ADR-1414; Identity ADR-1169; Identity ADR-1235</sub>
- **Make any invalid or hostile value from a remote party fail with the endpoint's defined client error (a 400 or protocol error such as `invalid_request`), never with an unhandled exception that becomes a 500. Catch the specific exceptions that conversion, strict decoding (`DecoderFallbackException`), DNS resolution of a user-supplied host (`ArgumentException` as well as `SocketException`) and thumbprint or descriptor calls throw for bad input.** A remote party controls these values, so any throwing conversion lets a caller trigger server errors instead of a defined rejection. *Check:* Look for parsing, arithmetic, decoding or DNS calls on untrusted values whose exceptions aren't mapped to the endpoint's error response or the method's documented exception type. <sub>Identity ADR-1123; Identity ADR-1266; Identity review of #420; Identity outcomes of #825</sub>
- **In an ASP.NET Core endpoint, catch `InvalidDataException` from `HttpRequest.ReadFormAsync` (a malformed or oversized body) and answer with the endpoint's usual 400 invalid-request error. In production code, read the form once, up front and before client authentication, through one shared helper.** Left uncaught, a client input error becomes a 500 and an error log entry. A shared reader keeps every endpoint consistent. *Check:* Look for ReadFormAsync calls without a catch for InvalidDataException, duplicated try-read-form helpers, or form reads after client authentication. <sub>Identity outcomes of #464; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **After deserializing a request body, check every property that must not be null, including `required` ones, and answer 400 before passing values to helpers that throw `ArgumentNullException`.** In System.Text.Json `required` only checks that the property is present, unless `RespectNullableAnnotations` is enabled, so an explicit null reaches a guard clause and the client gets a 500. *Check:* Look for request DTOs with `required` or non-nullable reference properties passed on without a null check, especially when a refactor replaced a null-tolerant comparison with a guarded helper. <sub>Identity outcomes of #724; Identity outcomes of #827</sub>
- **A Try-pattern method that reports refusals as `false` must never let an exception escape for input the caller sent. Check whether the input is supported before calling code that throws for unsupported input, or catch the documented exceptions. A `TryGet` lookup returns false only when the key is missing, and throws the same format exception as `Get` when the value is present with the wrong type.** An exception from a Try method breaks its contract and turns bad input into a 500, while treating a mistyped value as missing silently skips malformed data. *Check:* In Try* code, look for calls that can throw `NotSupportedException` or similar before the supported-type check, and TryGet implementations that return false on a type mismatch. <sub>Identity outcomes of #757; Randomness outcomes of #12</sub>
- **Don't swallow exceptions. A catch block must handle, translate, log or rethrow the error. A catch that deliberately ignores an exception needs a comment saying why that is safe, or must write the error to a warning or verbose stream. Never write `async void` in C#.** Swallowed errors hide failures that the change should surface. *Check:* Look for empty catch blocks, catch-all handlers that only return a default, ignored error results, `catch { $null = $_ }` without a comment or logging, and async void methods. <sub>Identity .github/agents/copilot-reviewer.agent.md; identity-platform .claude/commands/review-plan-diff.md; identity-platform .github/agents/copilot-reviewer.agent.md; project-template .claude/commands/review-plan-diff.md; project-template .github/agents/copilot-reviewer.agent.md; project-template outcomes of #183; Identity csharp.instructions.md</sub>
- **Decide a precondition (exists, unique, no dependents) from a fact the code queried, and have stores expose such facts as query methods. Answer 404 and 409 from rows read before the write. Never infer them by catching a broad store exception such as `InvalidOperationException` or `DbUpdateException` or from a save's return value. Catch only the specific exception that signals a race, such as a unique or foreign-key violation, and let other store failures propagate as 500.** Broad exceptions have many causes. Mapping them reads a store fault as a conflict, hides the real failure, and can trigger compensating actions such as destroying a newly created external key. *Check:* Look for try/catch around store calls in handlers that return NotFound or Conflict for a general exception type, and for conflict checks done only after side-effecting external calls. <sub>Identity ADR-1424; Identity ADR-1483; Identity outcomes of #686; Identity csharp.instructions.md</sub>
- **When translating exceptions into a domain exception or a 400 response, catch only the specific types the wrapped operation or dependency documents as refusals of bad input. Let everything else, including broad types such as `InvalidOperationException` and `PlatformNotSupportedException`, propagate unchanged to the logged 5xx path.** A broad filter turns bugs, SDK faults, outages or `OutOfMemoryException` into a refused key or bad request that callers act on wrongly, and it hides them from logs. *Check:* Look for `catch (Exception)` or `when ex is not ...` filters that rethrow as a domain exception, catches mapping broad types to 400, `PlatformNotSupportedException` merged into an invalid-key path, and KMS or SDK calls (`RpcException`, `RequestFailedException`) whose every failure becomes `CryptographicException`. *Note:* Don't report a catch-all translation when the interface contract documents that implementations fail only with that domain exception, the original is kept as InnerException, and a comment or tests pin it. <sub>Identity outcomes of #692; Identity outcomes of #699; Identity ADR-1068; Identity ADR-1260; Identity ADR-1476; Randomness outcomes of #12; Randomness outcomes of #13</sub>
- **Let an `OperationCanceledException` caused by the caller's token (including `HttpContext.RequestAborted`) propagate as is. Don't wrap it, report it as a timeout, turn it into an error response, retry, audit, or log it as an error. Document that a call already sent may still take effect. Treat an `OperationCanceledException` the caller did not request as a timeout or provider failure.** Cancellation is the contract's signal that the caller gave up or the client disconnected. It is neither a server fault nor a property of the input. *Check:* Look for catch blocks that catch `OperationCanceledException` without checking whether the caller's token was cancelled, wrap it in a custom exception, swallow it into a failure result, or log a request abort as an error or 500. <sub>Identity ADR-1167; Identity ADR-1280; Identity ADR-1315; Identity ADR-1290; coordination outcomes of #31; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Surface an outbound-call timeout from a resilience pipeline the way `HttpClient.Timeout` does: as a `TaskCanceledException` with a `TimeoutException` inner exception. Build the pipeline with the registered `TimeProvider`.** Callers tell timeouts from their own cancellation the same way for every client, and the injected TimeProvider keeps timing testable. *Check:* Look for Polly `TimeoutRejectedException` escaping to callers, other exception types for timeouts, and pipelines that use `TimeProvider.System` or the default instead of the one from DI. <sub>Identity ADR-1336; Identity ADR-1385</sub>
- **Give every outbound call to another service (HTTP, KMS, remote API, polling script) an explicit timeout and bounded retries with growing delay and jitter. Back off on HTTP 429 throttling instead of failing outright. In a polling script, treat a thrown connection or DNS error like a not-ready response until the deadline.** Without timeouts a hung call outlives its deadline. Unbounded or synchronized retries turn a dependency failure into a retry storm, and a single transient error shouldn't end a polling loop. *Check:* Look for HttpClient or remote calls without a timeout, `Invoke-RestMethod`/`Invoke-WebRequest` without `-TimeoutSec` or try/catch, retry loops with no attempt cap or fixed delays, and remote signers that fail on the first 429. <sub>Identity ADR-1134; Buffers outcomes of #59; Identity docs/hosting-analysis.md</sub>
- **Decide which exceptions count as an outbound fetch failure in one shared predicate. It covers timeouts, `HttpRequestException`, `IOException` and, with automatic decompression, corrupt bodies (`InvalidDataException`, `InvalidOperationException` from decompression streams), and it lets the caller's cancellation propagate. Keep decoding and parsing of the body outside the transport try block, and report status, content-type, size and malformed-document failures as themselves.** Duplicated filters drift. A too-narrow filter lets a corrupt body escape as a 500, and a too-broad one makes an invalid document look like a network failure. *Check:* Look for fetch catch filters copied across call sites, filters that list only some transport exceptions, and try blocks that contain decoding or parsing and classify every exception as a transport failure. <sub>Identity ADR-1315; Identity outcomes of #825; Randomness outcomes of #12</sub>
- **Scope each try block to the operation that its catch's error code or log message names. Give follow-up work, nested lazily evaluated values and per-item calls their own try, so a failure is reported against the part that actually failed.** A broad catch gives callers the wrong error code and points operators at the wrong component. *Check:* Look for one catch whose message describes one operation while its try also wraps removals, loops over items or lazily materialized nested conversions. <sub>Identity outcomes of #552; Identity outcomes of #577</sub>
- **When wrapping a caught exception in another exception, pass the original as the inner exception. When adding a more specific exception for a case already thrown as a base type, derive from that base type and add properties that identify the failing item.** The inner exception keeps diagnostic details such as the parser's position, and deriving from the base type keeps existing catch blocks working. *Check:* Look for catch blocks that throw a new exception built only from the caught exception's message, and for new exception types that replace a thrown base type without deriving from it. *Note:* Don't report a missing InnerException when the thrown type is unchanged, there is no underlying exception left to wrap, and the message carries the diagnostic details. <sub>Randomness outcomes of #13; Identity ADR-1245; Identity ADR-1012; Identity ADR-1285; Identity outcomes of #460</sub>
- **When recovery or cleanup runs after a failure, don't let it replace the original exception or result. Rethrow the original with the recovery failure attached (`ExceptionDispatchInfo`, `AggregateException`). Absorb the expected failure of a best-effort release in `finally` when the resource expires on its own anyway.** Otherwise the logs show the secondary failure instead of its cause, or a successfully fetched value is lost. *Check:* Look for catch blocks that call another fallible operation without a guarding try, and `finally` releases that can throw and replace the try block's outcome. <sub>Identity outcomes of #555; coordination outcomes of #22</sub>
- **When cleanup disposes an object and then a resource it depends on, dispose the object inside a try and release the resource in the finally.** If the first Dispose throws, sequential cleanup skips the second step and the resource leaks. *Check:* Look for several related Dispose or release calls in sequence with no try/finally between them. <sub>project-template outcomes of #189</sub>
- **When a multi-step acquire or create fails after an earlier step wrote shared or external state, undo that state on every failure path, cancellation included. Return a created external resource's identifier as soon as the service reports it, and hand it to one central destroyer if any later check fails. Treat a parse or import failure while verifying the returned resource as a failed check, destroy the resource, and throw the documented exception with the cause as inner exception.** A leftover registration blocks other parties, and an orphaned external key is billable and sensitive with no record pointing to it. *Check:* Follow every failure path after the first write in an acquire or create, including `OperationCanceledException` and verification steps such as importing a returned public key, and check that the write is undone. <sub>coordination outcomes of #22; Identity ADR-1471; Identity ADR-1474; Identity outcomes of #647</sub>
- **Run all validation, local conflict checks and preconditions before any side effect: before calling an external service or KMS, before reading the first row of a batch, before writing lasting state, before `GetSpan`/`Advance` on an `IBufferWriter<T>`, and before a shared flow that saves or audits. Check string lengths against the persisted column's maximum through a constant shared with the column configuration.** Failing after partial work leaves orphaned remote resources, half-applied configuration that later runs skip, or a caller's writer holding partial output. *Check:* Look for remote create or read calls, row loops, buffer advances or lasting writes that come before the validator or duplicate check, and length limits written as literals separate from the column's. <sub>Identity ADR-1476; Identity ADR-1471; Identity ADR-1408; Identity review of #375; project-template outcomes of #140; Identity ADR-1465; Identity outcomes of #572</sub>
- **After an operation has committed, run each follow-up step (announcement, cache eviction, refresh, audit publish, session termination, external resource destroy) independently: log a failure and continue with the rest, and never fail the committed operation. Put follow-up for items already committed in a `finally` so that a later failure or cancellation can't skip it, and run cleanup such as destroying external keys on its own bounded token rather than the caller's.** The change is durable. An error response makes the caller retry it, and a skipped eviction, announcement or destroy leaves stale caches, unaware replicas or leaked keys. *Check:* Look for post-commit sequences where one step's exception skips later steps or reaches the caller, evict or notify calls placed only after a per-item commit loop, cleanup using the request's CancellationToken, and failure logs missing the item identifiers. *Note:* Don't report an audit or event publish awaited after a commit when the publisher's contract isolates handler faults and sibling endpoints record audit the same way. <sub>Identity ADR-1205; Identity ADR-1351; Identity ADR-1404; Identity outcomes of #551; Identity outcomes of #553; Identity outcomes of #555; Identity outcomes of #647; Identity ADR-1478</sub>
- **When dispatching to several handlers or observers, wrap each handler in its own try/catch that logs, keep running the rest, and never surface a handler failure to the publisher. A failure recording an audit or observation event must never change the response. When a job has several handlers, reschedule it at most once per attempt.** A slow or broken sink must not break the operation or other sinks, and a retry per failing handler would run one failed attempt several times. *Check:* Look for loops that await handlers without per-handler try/catch, rethrow handler exceptions, put audit calls on the response path without a catch, or reschedule inside the per-handler catch. <sub>Identity ADR-1047; Identity ADR-1205; Identity docs/audit-records.md; Identity ADR-1242</sub>
- **In a background or batch pass over independent items (records, tenants, owners, providers), handle each item in its own try/catch that covers all of its work, including the store reads before it. Log the failure with the item's identity, skip it, and continue. Rethrow only cancellation of the stopping token, and report the pass as incomplete so it runs again. Never serve or reinterpret the skipped item.** One malformed item otherwise aborts the pass every tick, so the items after it are never processed, for example sessions that stay active. *Check:* Look for one try/catch around a whole loop, per-item awaits placed before the try, item exceptions that end the loop, and catches that don't log the item's id or that swallow the stopping token's cancellation. *Note:* A concurrency conflict lost to another replica during a prune counts as progress. Don't report counting a contended item as failed when an ADR records that choice. <sub>Identity ADR-1223; Identity ADR-1395; Identity ADR-1407; Identity ADR-1412; Identity ADR-1443; Identity ADR-1199; Identity outcomes of #545; Identity outcomes of #577; Identity outcomes of #599; Identity outcomes of #608; Identity outcomes of #702</sub>
- **In a `BackgroundService` or timer-driven hosted service, catch and log every failure of a run and retry after a delay or at the next tick. Exit `ExecuteAsync` only when the service's own stopping token is cancelled.** An escaping exception faults the service, stopping the host under `BackgroundServiceExceptionBehavior.StopHost` or ending the work for the life of the process. *Check:* Look at ExecuteAsync and PeriodicTimer loops that catch only specific types, or that catch OperationCanceledException without checking the stopping token. <sub>Identity ADR-1218; Identity outcomes of #608; Identity ADR-1443</sub>
- **On a request path, including list endpoints, let a malformed stored record fail the request that reads it. Never skip it in a listing.** Skipping a record hides it behind a listing that looks complete. On a request path the failure has a caller to reach. *Check:* Look for catch-and-continue or filter-out logic around deserializing stored records in request handlers and listings. *Note:* Background passes, which have no caller, log and skip instead (see the batch rule). Best-effort derived fields added to a management response after authorization may be omitted when the stored data behind them is unreadable. <sub>Identity ADR-1395; Identity ADR-1289</sub>
- **Don't cache a failure from lazy creation. Use `LazyThreadSafetyMode.PublicationOnly` for a `Lazy<T>` whose factory can fail transiently, or remove the cache entry when creation fails.** The default `ExecutionAndPublication` mode caches the exception, so the entry stays broken until restart. *Check:* Look for `Lazy<T>` or cached lazy entries with the default mode around factories that can throw. <sub>Identity outcomes of #584</sub>
- **When one change evicts several related caches, isolate each eviction (its own try/catch that logs, or the dependent eviction in a `finally`). When revalidation can't read current state, log a dedicated event and fall back to clearing every affected entry.** A failed first eviction or revalidation otherwise leaves stale entries in service. *Check:* Look for back-to-back `RemoveAsync` or clear calls with no isolation, and revalidation catch paths that keep cached entries. <sub>Identity outcomes of #555; Identity ADR-1416</sub>
- **Implement each rule that guards data once and call it from every entry point that accepts or consumes that data: startup configuration and reload, management API writes, imports, registration, seeders, alternative runners, and stored data on read. Reject an invalid value with the same outcome everywhere, and fail closed on stored data that fails it. In production code, express a cross-setting consistency rule as a registered rule (added with `TryAddEnumerable`) that a shared validator runs.** A check that only one path runs lets another path store or execute what the first refuses. *Check:* Check whether new validation is applied on only one path (for example config binding) while an API, seeder, plan file or persistence path that writes or runs the same value skips it, or whether a consistency check is written inline in one endpoint. <sub>Identity ADR-1140; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; project-template outcomes of #149; Identity ADR-1139</sub>
- **Give every validated setting a domain rule as well as a type: a closed string set is one-of, lifetimes and timeouts are positive, list elements are each validated and may not be null, and values a renderer consumes match the exact shape it reads (for example `#rgb`/`#rrggbb`, absolute `https` URIs, bounded text with no control characters). Report a null collection and a null entry with their own messages.** A value of the right type that the server can't honor slips through, and a null or misspelled list entry can silently narrow a ceiling to nothing. *Check:* Look for new settings without a domain rule, lists validated only as a whole, null entries reported as an unknown empty name, and presentation settings that accept free-form values. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity ADR-1140; Identity ADR-1253; Identity outcomes of #547</sub>
- **Validate configuration the way it will be used, and reject a value that parses to something other than what was written. `IPAddress.TryParse`, `IPNetwork.TryParse` and `Uri.TryCreate` are lenient, so require canonical forms: a dotted-quad IPv4, a CIDR whose address is the network address, an explicit `scheme:` without whitespace, and a CORS origin with only scheme, host and optional port. Exclude Kestrel `pipe` and `unix` hosts when classifying TCP endpoints.** Lenient parsers turn typos into other values, the binder reads enums from numbers, and `Uri` gives a named-pipe address a default port. *Check:* Look for options validation that relies only on TryParse or TryCreate succeeding, enum options without Enum.IsDefined, values stored normalized when they are compared verbatim, and endpoint classification by `Uri.Port`. <sub>Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity ADR-1447; Identity ADR-1370; Identity outcomes of #787</sub>
- **Validate configuration that would otherwise fail on first use (unknown strategy names, route templates missing a parameter, uncompilable patterns, malformed URLs, conflicting endpoint metadata) before the host starts, with `ValidateOnStart` or at endpoint mapping. Don't validate it lazily on the request path or inside a hosted service's loop.** A late failure comes after health checks reported the instance ready, or it faults one background service while the host keeps serving. *Check:* Look for options parsed or checked on the request path or in a run loop instead of in a startup validator, and options bound without ValidateOnStart. *Note:* A requirement on a dependency that needs request services can only be checked when it is used. - **A startup or precondition check collects every failure and throws one `InvalidOperationException` that lists them all, names each failing item, and names the registration, call or command that fixes it. Run it before any work starts, and give it no bypass switch.** The operator fixes everything in one pass instead of restarting once per problem. *Check:* Look for validation loops that throw on the first bad item, messages that omit the failing item or the fix, and checks that run after resources have started. <sub>Identity ADR-1071; Identity ADR-1433; Identity ADR-1504; Identity outcomes of #548</sub>
- **Validate a registered set of named descriptors, handlers or strategies as a whole when it is composed. Throw an exception naming the culprit for a null entry, an empty or whitespace name (`string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace`), a duplicate name or selector, a dangling reference or a cycle. Answer with `invalid_client_metadata`.** Metadata the server can't honor must fail at registration, not at the first token request, and what the provider does must match what it advertises (RFC 7523, RFC 8705, OpenID Connect Core §8.1). *Check:* Look at registration and update validation for missing checks of membership in the supported list, required key material, `_enc`/`_alg` pairing, multi-host pairwise clients, and settings tied to disabled capabilities. <sub>Identity ADR-1088; Identity ADR-1093; Identity ADR-1145; Identity ADR-1155; Identity ADR-1192; Identity ADR-1391</sub>
- **Validate that a key matches its declared JOSE algorithm (type, size, curve) when the key is registered, imported or provisioned. Reject generation parameters that don't apply to the key type, such as a size that conflicts with the named curve or a curve passed to an RSA or symmetric generator. When an import or update repeats the JWK's `kid`, `use` or `alg`, refuse values that contradict them.** A mismatched key or meaningless parameter is a configuration error that should be refused up front, not when the key is first used. *Check:* Look for key registration, import, generation or update paths that accept a key/algorithm pair without the runtime's compatibility check, silently ignore a supplied curve, or let request metadata override the JWK's own. <sub>Identity ADR-1389; Identity ADR-1068; Identity ADR-1161; Identity ADR-1392</sub>
- **When DPoP or another required binding cannot be applied, throw before sending anything: `InvalidOperationException` for a client configuration problem, and a provider exception when the provider advertises no usable algorithm.** A required binding must never fall back to an unbound request. *Check:* Look at required-binding paths that send the request without a proof or throw the wrong kind of exception. <sub>Identity ADR-1286</sub>
- **Answer a refresh whose spend finds the grant missing or no longer active, including a spend lost to a concurrent request, exactly like a reused revoked refresh token: `invalid_grant`, the reuse policy applied, and the token family revoked. On the client side, end the session only on `invalid_grant`. Answer other OAuth errors with 502 and transport failures or timeouts with 503.** RFC 9700 §4.14.2 requires a lost race to be treated as reuse, and only `invalid_grant` means the grant is dead. Outages must not end a user's session. *Check:* Look for a null or false conditional spend that throws a 500, issues tokens or skips reuse handling, and for client refresh handling that treats every failure as session end or `invalid_grant` as transient. <sub>Identity ADR-1216; Identity ADR-1291</sub>
- **When calling a key management service, map only the status that means a wrong ciphertext, key or context (such as HTTP 400 or gRPC `InvalidArgument`) to `CryptographicException`, an integrity mismatch in the response to `IOException`, and an unreadable key identifier to `ArgumentException`. Throw `NotSupportedException` for an operation the provider never offers and `InvalidOperationException` for one its configuration can't run. At an API, answer KMS refusals with 400 and log and answer other KMS failures with 502. Make destroy succeed when the key is already missing, disabled or scheduled for deletion.** The exception type tells callers whether to retry and whether the caller or the upstream service is at fault, and destroy must be safe to repeat. *Check:* Look for KMS catches that turn every failure into `CryptographicException`, 500 answers, refusals treated as 502 or the reverse, missing provider and secret identifiers in logs, and destroy implementations that throw on not-found. *Note:* Don't ask to narrow a decrypt 400/InvalidArgument mapping when the provider verifies the key's algorithm and operations before storing it and reports disabled or deleted keys with other statuses. <sub>Identity ADR-1260; Identity ADR-1474; Identity ADR-1476; Identity outcomes of #702</sub>
- **Report any asymmetry between code paths meant to behave alike (parallel paths, sibling modules, read/write, encode/decode, producer/consumer): validation, error handling, logging or edge-case handling present in one and missing from the other.** Such an asymmetry is a gap that leaves the capability delivered inconsistently. *Check:* Compare the changed path with its counterpart for argument validation, failure modes, logging and edge cases, and flag whatever one has and the other lacks without a stated reason. <sub>NCodeGroup maintainer: gap-hunting-review</sub>
- **Trace each capability a change delivers down to its implementation, and handle every failure path: null, empty and boundary inputs, large inputs, off-by-one bounds, concurrent access, failing or timed-out dependencies, invariant violations, and release of every acquired resource on every path. Report a missing case as an in-scope gap even when the ticket didn't name it.** Closing such a gap completes the existing capability, and production code can't rely on fragile assumptions about its inputs. *Check:* For each new external call, check for a timeout and failure handling. For each public entry point, check null and invalid arguments. Check loop bounds, unsynchronized shared state, undisposed resources, and failures that are silent or unobservable. <sub>NCodeGroup maintainer: gap-hunting-review; NCodeGroup maintainer: principal-engineer-review; project-template .claude/commands/review-code.md</sub>
- **Don't null-check a non-nullable member that always has a default instance. Drop the check or make the declared nullability match it.** The check hides the contract that the value is always present. *Check:* Look for `is not null` or `!= null` on members declared non-nullable with a default initializer. <sub>Identity outcomes of #606</sub>
- **Don't report a catch, deviation or fail-open/fail-closed choice that a comment on the code or a decision record explicitly documents, such as a stream ended quietly under a delivery guarantee that allows it, or a contended item counted as failed.** The behavior is intended and documented, and the maintainer has declined such findings. *Check:* Before reporting, read the comment on the catch and the ADRs the code or feature cites, and check whether a stricter mode still fails. <sub>Identity outcomes of #553; coordination outcomes of #21</sub>
- **Don't report other intended patterns as defects: a BCL behavior on other target frameworks when the project targets one framework and a test pins the behavior; an inline entity-specific check that maps a lower layer's rule to a precise 400 while the shared validator serves entities with different limits; case-insensitive dedup of identifiers the store normalizes; `(int)response.StatusCode` in an HTTP error message; a dedicated configuration exception that doesn't derive from `InvalidOperationException` when no convention requires it; a missing timeout or catch around a final cleanup call into a caller-supplied handler; or a `Test-Path` on a path from `git worktree list`, which can list prunable worktrees whose folders are gone.** Each is deliberate, and the maintainers declined these findings. *Check:* Before raising one of these, confirm the condition that makes it intended: a single TargetFramework and pinning test, the other callers of the shared validator, how the store keys identifiers, whether the typed status is still on the exception, a convention or ADR requiring the base type, whether the callee is caller code, or whether the path comes from a listing that can be stale. <sub>Buffers outcomes of #124; Identity outcomes of #463; Identity outcomes of #585; Randomness outcomes of #13; coordination outcomes of #18; coordination outcomes of #22; project-template outcomes of #354</sub>
